State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
B.M., India First Life Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Rohini Bai on 14 November, 2023
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
 FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai

 AFR / NAFR
 CHHATTISGARH STATE
 CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION
 PANDRI, RAIPUR

 Date of Institution: 04/06/2020
 Date of Final Hearing: 18/10/2023
 Date of Pronouncement: 14/11/2023

 APPEAL No.- FA/20/259
 IN THE MATTER OF :
 The Branch Manager,
 India First Life Insurance Company Limited,
 Add.: Bank of Baroda Akaltara,
 Dist. JANJGIR - CHAMPA (C.G.)
 Registered Office: India First Life Insurance Company Limited,
 12th / 13th Floor, North (C) Wing, Tower 4, Nesco IT Park,
 Nesco Center, Western Express Highway, Goregaon (East)
 MUMBAI - 400 063
 ... Appellant
 Through: Shri Saurabh Shukla, Advocate
 Vs.
 Smt. Rohini Bai W/o. Late Rajababu,
 Add.: Ward No.11, Nahar Para, Vill. Tarod, Tah. Akaltara,
 Dist. JANJGIR - CHAMPA (C.G.)
 ... Respondent.
 Through : Shri Dhanendra Soni, Advocate

 CORAM: -
 HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE GAUTAM CHOURDIYA, PRESIDENT
 HON'BLE SHRI PRAMOD KUMAR VARMA, MEMBER
PRESENT: -
Shri Saurabh Shukla, Advocate, for the appellant.
 Shri Dhanendra Soni, Advocate for the respondent.
J U DGE M E NT
 PER: - JUSTICE GAUTAM CHOURDIYA, PRESIDENT

 This appeal, filed under
Section 15
of the Consumer Protection Act

 1986 (hereinafter called "the Act" for short) is directed against order dated

 13/12/2019 passed by District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum,

 Janjgir-Champa (C.G.) (hereinafter referred to as "District Forum" for

 short), in Complaint Case No.CC/11/2019, whereby the complaint filed

 by the respondent herein alleging deficiency in service against the

 appellants herein in repudiating her insurance claim was partly allowed

 and the appellants were directed to pay within a month the sum assured

 of Rs.5,00,000/- (Five Lacs) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of
Dismissed Page 1 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
compliant i.e. 30.01.2019, compensation for mental agony Rs.10,000/- (Ten

 Thousand) and cost of litigation Rs.2,000/- (Two Thousand). Feeling

 aggrieved, the opposite party insurance company has preferred this

 appeal.
2. In nutshell the facts of the case are that indisputably the husband of

 the complainant Late Rajababu obtained a life insurance policy from the

 appellant/ opposite party on 14.03.2015 for sum assured of Rs.5,00,000/-

 (Five Lacs). During subsistence of the policy on 07.01.2017 the insured

 husband of the respondent / complainant died. As per case of the

 respondent/ complainant she preferred claim before the appellant /

 insurance company in the month of April 2017, which was repudiated.

 Legal notice was also sent but the same was not replied nor the amount of

 insurance claim was paid hence alleging deficiency in service on the part

 of the appellant/ opposite party insurance company, complaint was filed

 seeking direction for payment of sum assured of Rs.5,00,000/- (Five Lacs),

 compensation for mental agony Rs.1,00,000/- (One Lac) along with cost of

 litigation and any other relief.
3. The appellant / opposite party insurance company filed its written

 version before the District Forum mainly to the effect that the life assured

 was chronic alcoholic and suffering from ascites with cirrhosis of liver

 disease, he was taking treatment for the same. He was first diagnosed for

 ascites and positive cirrhosis of liver on 03.10.2011, which was prior to the

 issuance of insurance policy but this material information was suppressed

 at the time of filling proposal form for insurance which amounts to breach

 of principle of uberrima fides hence the insurance claim was repudiated, in

 which the insurance company has not committed any deficiency in

 service.
Dismissed Page 2 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
4. Learned District Forum on consideration of rival contentions of

 both parties partly allowed the complaint and directed the appellant/

 opposite party to pay the sum assured, compensation for mental agony

 and cost of litigation as aforesaid in paragraph No.1.
5. We have heard final arguments of both parties, perused the record

 and the written arguments submitted by learned counsel for the

 respondent / complainant.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant / opposite party has filed certain

 document as per list along with an application under order 41 rule 27
of

 CPC
, marked as I.A. No.01/2023, which has already been allowed and

 documents are taken on record. Along with the application the documents

 filed are photocopy of Liver Function Test of the deceased dated

 31.10.2011, his treatment records of 2016 and 2017, letter of repudiation

 and investigation report, death certificate etc. whereas most of them were

 already filed before the District Forum and were considered.
7. Before us the appellant/ opposite party has reiterated the facts

 stated and grounds taken in the written version and argued that the

 learned District Forum has erred in appreciating the terms of the policy,

 information filled in the proposal form by the deceased life assured and

 his treatment records in the light of
Section 45
of the Insurance Act, 1938

 and has passed an erroneous order, hence this appeal needs to be allowed

 setting aside the impugned order. Whereas the learned counsel for the

 respondent/ complainant has supported the impugned order and argued

 that learned District Commission has rightly held the appellant/ opposite

 party deficient in service in repudiating the genuine claim of the
Dismissed Page 3 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
respondent/ complainant and passed the impugned order which is just

 and proper and is not required to be interfered with.
8. We have considered the arguments advanced by both parties and

 gone through the record as well as the impugned order. In the impugned

 order we find that learned District Commission has arrived at the

 conclusion that the appellant/ opposite party has failed to establish that

 the insured had fraudulently concealed any information of his previous

 disease. It is true that in the proposal form the deceased Rajababu gave all

 the answers in negative but at the same time it is also true that he was not

 having knowledge of any pre-existing disease as appears from the

 available documents in the record of the District Forum as well as the

 documents filed before us. Only two documents i.e. Abdominal Ultra

 Sonography Report dated 03.10.2011, filed before the District Forum as

 Exhibit OP-3 and photocopy of Liver Function Test of the deceased dated

 31.10.2011 are the documents of some diagnostic tests only which were

 done about four and half years prior the date of proposal for insurance.

 But what were the final findings, what treatment was given, which

 medicines were prescribed and for which period, to clarify these facts no

 document is brought on record. Whether the deceased Rajababu had to

 stay admitted in any hospital for treatment, nothing of that sort is proved

 by the appellant / opposite party by way of filing any cogent evidence.
9. The appellant / opposite party has also brought on record the

 Death Claim Investigation Report of Eagle Eye Consultant Private

 Limited, which is marked as Exhibit OP-4. In the said investigation report

 except mere description and opinion of the investigator nothing was

 discussed on the basis of which such opinion was given nor any evidence

 was filed along with the said investigation report. In the said report
Dismissed Page 4 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
nowhere it is specifically stated that the deceased underwent any

 treatment and remained admitted in any hospital for a period more than a

 week or even for a single day. It is also not specifically mentioned that

 any medicine was continuously being taken by the life assured since 2011

 till the date of proposal, instead it is mentioned that local doctors failed to

 indentify the life assured by name. At the conclusion, only it is mentioned

 that as per information given life assured visited Mission Hospital

 Bilaspur few years back, where the doctors suggested him to stop

 alcoholism, but such document was not brought on record. At the

 appellate stage the insurance company itself has brought on record a

 document titled as „Physician‟s Statement - Death‟ as Annexure-5 in

 which in second page under „Prior Medical History‟ in reply to the

 question „Have you advised the deceased during the past 5 years, prior to

 the final illness? the check box given against „No‟ was ticked, meaning

 thereby the Medical Officer of District Hospital Janjgir has certified that

 the life assured was never advised by him in the past 5 years. This

 document also goes against the case of the appellant/ insurance company.

 Thus, from the documents available on record of the District Forum as

 well as filed before us we are not convinced that the deceased was having

 any pre-existing disease or he was taking any medicine. In fact the

 insurance company has also failed to prove that the life assured was

 having knowledge of any pre-existing disease, which he suppressed in the

 proposal form for obtaining his life insurance.
10. So far as the another ground of repudiation of claim that the life

 assured was alcoholic is concerned, in the Discharge Ticket, Annexure-6,

 dated 27.12.2016 the name of illness is mentioned as chronic alcoholic liver

 disease with ascites with severe anaemia. The policy in question was
Dismissed Page 5 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
obtained on 14.03.2015 and on 27.12.2016 i.e. after about one year and

 more than nine months, it was diagnosed that the life assured was chronic

 alcoholic. The approximate period reported by the life assured or any

 other source is not mentioned to determine as to for how long the life

 assured was alcoholic and this ambiguous situation is not sufficient to

 hold that the life assured was alcoholic prior to the date of proposal, hence

 this ground of repudiation of claim also has no leg to stand. Hence, with

 the foregoing discussion we are of the considered view that the appellant

 / opposite party insurance company has committed deficiency in service

 in repudiating the insurance claim of the life assured deceased husband of

 the complainant, as has rightly been held by the learned District Forum.
11. Learned counsel for the appellant / opposite party insurance

 company has placed reliance upon judgements of Hon‟ble Apex Court in
P.C. Chacko & Anr. Vs. Chairman Life Insurance Corporation of India

 & Anr.
, (2008) 1 SCC 231;
Life Insurance Corporation of India & Ors. Vs.

 Asha Goel (Smt.) & Anr.
, (2001) 2 SCC 160; United India Insurance Co.

 Ltd. Vs. MKJ Corporation in Appeal (Civil) No.6075-6076 of 1995 dated

 21.08.1996 and that of Hon‟ble National Commission in
Life Insurance

 Corporation of India Vs. Smt. Kusum Patro, II
(2012) CPJ 272 (NC) in

 support of his arguments that principle of utmost good faith was breached

 by the life assured hence the insurance company has right to repudiate the

 insurance claim, whereas learned counsel for the respondent /

 complainant has
placed reliance upon
judgement of Hon‟ble Apex Court

 in
Santwant Kaur Sandhu Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Civil

 Appeal No.2776
of 2002 dated 10.07.2009. But the case laws relied by

 learned counsel for the appellant / opposite party as well as the

 respondent / complainant are not relevant in the facts of the instant case
Dismissed Page 6 of 7
Appeal Nos.: Branch Manager, India First Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Date of Pronouncement:
FA/20/259 Vs. 14/11/2023
 Smt. Rohini Bai
as the appellant insurance company has failed to prove its contention, as

 discussed hereinabove, that any material information regarding previous

 treatment, pre-existing disease or consumption of alcohol prior to the date

 of making proposal for life insurance was concealed deliberately by the

 life assured. Hence, we are of the considered view that the appellant /

 opposite party has committed deficiency in service in repudiating the

 insurance claim as has rightly been held by learned District Forum.
12. So far as the quantum of award is concerned learned District

 Forum has justifiably awarded the sum assured under the insurance

 policy in question and the amount of compensation for mental agony also

 appears justified in the facts and circumstances of the case and calls for no

 interference.
13. Therefore, in view of the above discussion, we do not find any error

 in the impugned order passed by learned District Forum, hence we affirm

 the same and dismiss this appeal being devoid of any merit. No order as

 to cost.
(Justice Gautam Chourdiya) (Pramod Kumar Varma)
 President Member
 /11/2023 /11/2023

 Pronounced On: 14th November 2023
Dismissed Page 7 of 7
